entrypoints.summary: The GET messages endpoint accepts q together with filterQueryType=GROOVY_SCRIPT; the disclosure supplies a complete request example.
The project advisory identifies q at /api/clusters/local/topics/{topic}/messages as the arbitrary-code execution input.

affected_components.role: Selects the GROOVY_SCRIPT filter path and evaluates compiled Groovy while testing topic messages.

causal_paths.kind: http query to server-side script evaluation

code_slices.surrounding_context: The version-pinned source page identifies MessageFilters.java at commit 53a6553765a806eda9905c43bfcfe09da6812035; no fixed code slice is present.
code_slices.vulnerable: GROOVY_SCRIPT dispatches to groovyScriptFilter; the disclosed implementation compiles supplied script and invokes compiledScript.eval(bindings) while testing a message.

negative_controls: The disclosure does not provide an observed execution result for a patched build.
The file is not expected until the filter is evaluated against a topic message.
observability.positive_marker: Creation of /tmp/pwnd.txt on the Kafka UI server.

preconditions: Kafka UI is running and connected to a Kafka cluster.
A topic has a message available for evaluation, or a new message is sent after the filter is installed.
If authentication is enabled, the disclosure states an attacker needs a valid account; Kafka UI authentication is noted as disabled by default.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A URL-encoded Groovy expression that invokes ProcessBuilder("touch", "/tmp/pwnd.txt").start().
trigger_steps.summary: Request topic messages with filterQueryType=GROOVY_SCRIPT and place a ProcessBuilder expression in q.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A topic message serving as the predicate-evaluation trigger.
trigger_steps.summary: Cause filter evaluation against an existing or subsequently delivered topic message.

capabilities.concept: Server-side evaluation of attacker-supplied unsandboxed Groovy

impacts.concept: Remote code execution in Kafka UI server process

relation_candidates.dst: Server-side evaluation of attacker-supplied unsandboxed Groovy

The disclosure's Groovy payload invokes ProcessBuilder.start(), and identifies the filter as unsandboxed.

impact.affected_asset: Kafka UI server host/process and its accessible filesystem or other resources available to that process.
impact.attacker_capability: Execute an attacker-selected operating-system command when a topic message is evaluated against the supplied Groovy filter.
impact.security_effect: Remote arbitrary code execution in the Kafka UI server process, characterized by the disclosure as post-auth RCE; deployments without enabled authentication are especially exposed.

causal_trace.summary: An HTTP client supplies a Groovy expression in q and selects the GROOVY_SCRIPT filter type on message retrieval.
A message filter that should operate as a predicate over message data accepts arbitrary Groovy source without sandboxing.
MessageFilters selects groovyScriptFilter for GROOVY_SCRIPT; that path compiles attacker-controlled script and evaluates the compiled script with bindings while testing a topic message.
A supplied ProcessBuilder expression can start an operating-system command in the Kafka UI server process; the documented example creates a server-side file.

failure.operation: Compiled Groovy script evaluation during message predicate testing, permitting ProcessBuilder.start()

primary_invariant.statement: User-provided message filters must be restricted to data-filtering behavior and must not execute arbitrary server-process code.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Selecting GROOVY_SCRIPT routes the q value to compilation and evaluation of unsandboxed Groovy in the server process.

quality.review_notes: Primary disclosure documents the request, vulnerable evaluation operation, prerequisite that a topic contain a message (or receive one), and filesystem oracle. No execution transcript was inspected, so the oracle is a documented reproduction contract rather than an observed run. Authentication remains deployment-qualified: the disclosure calls this post-auth RCE while noting authentication is disabled by default. A v0.7.2 release is named, but no patch diff or fixed source was supplied, so exact remediation mechanics remain uncertain.

remediation.invariant_restored: The disclosure identifies v0.7.2 as the release containing the fix; the available bundle does not include an inspectable patch showing the exact code-level restriction or removal of Groovy evaluation.

oracle.channel: server-side filesystem observation after HTTP message request
oracle.expected_negative: A remediated deployment should not create the requested file from that filter input.
oracle.expected_positive: Against the documented vulnerable configuration with an existing topic message, a GROOVY_SCRIPT request containing the disclosed ProcessBuilder touch expression creates /tmp/pwnd.txt on the server.
